evidence.title: Perceived speedup differs from measured completion time
evidence.observation: After the trial, developers estimated that AI reduced completion time by 20%, despite the measured slowdown.
evidence.evidence_standing: Author-reported bounded survey and trial; not independently reproduced by the Commons
evidence.limitations: The same participants and trial underlie both records. Perception mismatch alone does not demonstrate deception, lost competence, or organizational dependency.
evidence.open_questions: Does assurance need a direct outcome measure when perceived usefulness and elapsed time diverge?
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed summary of the cited author or provider account. Source inspection supports traceability; the Commons has not independently replicated or verified the underlying finding.

terms.name: Assurance
terms.definition: Evidence-supported confidence that specified properties or outcomes will hold under stated objectives, operating conditions, and assumptions. Assurance has a defined scope and can lose relevance when those conditions change.

terms.name: Outcome–purpose divergence
terms.definition: A condition in which meeting an immediate objective or metric degrades the benefit or purpose that justified pursuing it. The divergence can occur through narrow measures or indirect consequences without an intent to deceive.

relationships.explanation: Perceived speed is insufficient evidence for a specified elapsed-time outcome; evidence must match the claimed property.
Measured time differs from perceived benefit, but the study does not establish a hidden shift in the intended purpose.

source_dependencies.explanation: Author blog and paper abstract report one trial; they are not two independent confirmations.
